title: Classification and phylogeny; Evidence for evolution; Polygenic and environmental variation; Adaptations
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV06c#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV06c#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV06b#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV06c#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV03a#N.5a, EV03b#N.7a, EV06b#N.3, EV06c#N.7, EV09#N.3, IN07#N.2, EV03a#N.7a, EV06b#N.6, EV09#N.14, IN07#N.9, EV03a#N.12b, EV09#N.18.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Domain
items.clue: Level of classification above kingdom; life has three

items.label: Eukarya
items.clue: Top-level group containing Protoctista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia

items.label: Common ancestor
items.clue: Shared more recently by relatives whose base sequences show fewer differences

items.label: Ribosomal RNA
items.clue: Molecule whose base sequences Woese and Fox compared across many organisms in 1977

questions.stem: The amino acid sequence of the same protein was compared in four species. Compared with species W, species X differs at 2 positions, species Y at 15 positions and species Z at 31 positions. Which conclusion is supported by the data?

options.text: W shares a more recent common ancestor with X than it does with either Y or Z.
Z is the most primitive of the four species, because its sequence is furthest from W's.
X lives in the same kind of habitat as W, because similar conditions give similar proteins.
X is the ancestor of W, because the two sequences are almost identical.

questions.explanation: Differences accumulate after two lineages split. W and X differ least, so their common ancestor is the most recent.

questions.stem: Cabbage, kale, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi and Brussels sprouts were all produced from wild cabbage (Brassica oleracea) by selective breeding over the past few thousand years. What does this show about evolution?

options.text: Breeders were able to produce each new characteristic by causing the mutation that was needed for it.
The heritable characteristics of a population can change greatly in a short time when selection is strong.
It is not evidence of evolution, because the changes were brought about by humans rather than by nature.
Each variety has now become a separate species, because the varieties differ so much in their appearance.

questions.stem: Using the cytochrome c data, which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Humans evolved from chimpanzees, because their cytochrome c sequences are identical.
Humans share a more recent common ancestor with the dog than with the tuna.
The tuna is the least evolved of these animals, because its protein differs most from ours.
The dog and the chicken differ from each other at 2 positions, since 13 − 11 = 2.

questions.explanation: 11 differences against 21. Differences accumulate after lineages split, so fewer differences mean a more recent common ancestor.

questions.stem: Which evidence was used in 1977 to propose that all organisms should be classified into three domains?

options.text: Visible differences in cell structure seen using the electron microscope.
Evidence that archaea are a subgroup of bacteria, so that all prokaryotes form one domain.
Overall similarity in the appearance and way of life of the organisms being classified.
Comparison of the base sequences of ribosomal RNA across many different organisms.

questions.explanation: rRNA base sequences showed that prokaryotes form two groups, each as different from the other as from eukaryotes.

options.text: A rattlesnake's venom is an anatomical adaptation, because it is delivered through the fangs.
Zebras living in herds is not an adaptation, because behaviour is not inherited.
A kangaroo rat producing very concentrated urine is a physiological adaptation.
A dog moved to a cold country growing a thicker coat during its life is an anatomical adaptation.

questions.explanation: It is a body process, carried out by the kidneys, that saves water in the desert.

questions.stem: Identical twins have the same genotype. Two identical twins were raised apart, one in a sunny country on a good diet and the other in a cloudy country on a poor diet. Which of these traits are expected to be the same in both twins as adults: ABO blood group, adult height and skin colour?

options.text: ABO blood group, but neither adult height nor skin colour
ABO blood group and adult height, but not skin colour
ABO blood group and skin colour, though not adult height
ABO blood group, adult height and skin colour

questions.explanation: Identical twins have the same alleles, so ABO blood group, due to genotype only, is the same in both. Height depends on nutrition during growth and skin colour on sunlight, as well as on alleles, so both are expected to differ.

questions.stem: A copy of the human insulin gene, with its introns removed, was inserted into a bacterium, which then made a polypeptide with the same amino acid sequence as the human one. Which conclusion does this best support, and why?

options.text: Humans and bacteria share the same genes, because the bacterium already carried all the information needed to make human insulin.
The genetic code is shared by humans and bacteria, because the bacterium translated human triplets into the same amino acids.
The bacterium adopted the human genetic code in place of its own bacterial code when the human gene was inserted.
Any organism could translate any gene, because the code we observe is the only one that is chemically possible.

questions.stem: On a cladogram, the root leads to node 1, where species P branches off. Node 2 separates species Q from the remaining species. Node 3 separates species R from species S and T, which are joined at node 4. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Q is more closely related to R than to T, because Q and R branch at adjacent nodes.
P is the most primitive of the five species, because it branches off nearest the root.
R shares a more recent common ancestor with S than it shares with Q.
Q, R and S form a clade, and so do Q, R, S and T taken together as a group.

questions.explanation: R joins S at node 3, but joins Q further back at node 2. Node 3 is more recent, so R is more closely related to S.

questions.stem: Cacti of the deserts of the Americas and euphorbias of the deserts of southern Africa both have swollen, water-storing stems and spines, yet they belong to different plant families. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: The similar appearance shows that cacti and euphorbias share a recent common ancestor that spread to both continents.
Hot desert is one biome, so its community is the same on every continent and each plant in it has the desert form.
Individual plants of any family develop spines and swollen stems when they grow in dry conditions during their lifetime.
Similar abiotic conditions selected for similar adaptations in unrelated lineages, an example of convergent evolution.

questions.stem: Human skin colour varies continuously across a population, whereas ABO blood group falls into four separate classes. Which explanation of this difference is correct?

options.text: Skin colour is controlled by one gene with a very large number of alleles, whereas the blood group gene has only three alleles
Skin colour is determined by the environment only, with no genetic contribution, whereas blood group is determined by genotype only
Both are continuous variables, since each can be sorted into several categories; skin colour simply has more of them
Skin colour depends on several genes and on sunlight, giving many grades; blood group depends on one gene with discrete alleles

questions.stem: Three hypothetical beetle species are compared. Species A and C look almost identical; species B looks quite different. Illustrative genomic DNA data: A and B differ at 0.8% of aligned bases, A and C at 6.1%, and B and C at 6.0%. Which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: A and C are the closest relatives, because species that look so alike must share the most recent common ancestor.
A and B share the most recent common ancestor; A and C look alike for another reason.
B evolved from A, because their DNA sequences are so nearly identical.
C is the most primitive species, because its DNA differs most from the other two.

questions.stem: Arctic foxes have much smaller ears than fennec foxes. Which statement best explains how small ears became typical of Arctic foxes?

options.text: Each Arctic fox's ears shrank during its life in the cold, and its cubs inherited the smaller ears.
Foxes with alleles for smaller ears lost less heat, so survived and bred more; the alleles spread.
The cold caused new mutations for small ears to arise in the foxes that needed them.
Small ears are better in every environment, so in time all foxes will evolve them.
